w: Pluckley sits in the soft Kent Weald like a village that prefers to keep its secrets. The church of St Nicholas stands slightly apart, its graveyard sloping gently under yew and cedar. Most visitors pass through unaware of the weight in the air. The stories are specific and local. At Fright Corner a highwayman was ambushed and killed; his shade is still seen among the trees. In the churchyard two ladies — one red, one white — are said to walk at dusk. A gypsy woman drowned in a nearby stream, a miller continues his work, and terrible screams rise from Dering Wood. Some tales trace back to real, unhappy deaths; others grew in the telling across generations. Walk the lanes as the light fades. Stand in the churchyard when the rooks settle. Listen in the wood. Whether you meet anything uncanny is almost beside the point. The place has already made you slow down and wonder what else the landscape remembers.
